draft.title: The inflation target
card: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general level of prices. The RBA measures it as the yearly percentage change in the consumer price index (CPI), which tracks the cost of a typical basket of household goods and services.

The RBA aims to keep inflation between 2 and 3% a year, on average, over time. This is a target for the medium term, so inflation can sit outside the band for a while without the target being given up.
The RBA also aims for full employment, meaning jobs for everyone who wants to work. Low and stable inflation supports this, because people and firms can plan and invest when prices are predictable.
The target is not zero inflation. Inflation that is too high erodes the value of money and savings, and inflation that is too low can signal weak spending.
draft.remember: The RBA aims for inflation of 2 to 3% on average, together with full employment.

a.q: Which statement best describes the RBA's inflation target?
opts: Keep inflation between 2 and 3% a year on average over time
Keep inflation at exactly 2% in every quarter
Keep prices from rising at all, so inflation stays at zero
Keep inflation under 3%, with no lower limit
a.why: The target is a band of 2 to 3% reached on average over the medium term, so short spells outside it do not break it. A target of exactly 2% every quarter is wrong because the band allows some movement and the focus is on the average.
a.clue: The target is a band, measured over time.

b.q: Over the past year, Australia's CPI rose by 3.6%. The RBA's target band is 2 to 3%. Which conclusion fits the target?
opts: Inflation is above the band, so the aim is not met now
Inflation is within the band, so the aim is met now
Inflation is below the band, so the aim is not met now
The target is given up whenever inflation leaves the band
b.why: 3.6% is above 3%, so inflation is currently above the band and the aim is not being met at present. It is not given up, because the target is about the average over time and the RBA still aims to bring inflation back into the band.
b.clue: Compare 3.6% with the top of the band.

a.best: Keep inflation between 2 and 3% a year on average over time

b.best: Inflation is above the band, so the aim is not met now

problems.detail: Full employment is defined as 'jobs for everyone who wants to work', which suggests zero unemployment. In HSC Economics, full employment is the lowest unemployment rate consistent with stable inflation, the natural rate or NAIRU, so frictional and structural unemployment remain. The RBA calls this the maximum sustainable level of employment. Year 12 students could take away a wrong definition.

The question only asks students to compare 3.6% with 3%. The clue 'Compare 3.6% with the top of the band' then all but names the answer. This is too easy for Year 12 and tests arithmetic rather than the idea of a medium-term target.

'The aim is not met now' sits awkwardly with the card's point that the target is judged on average over time. Saying inflation is currently above the target band would be more precise and would not suggest the target is failed by one year's reading.

b.q: Annual CPI inflation in Australia reaches 3.6%, after several years near 2.5%. Has the RBA given up its inflation target?
opts: No, the target is an average over the medium term
Yes, the target is broken once inflation leaves the band

Yes, the RBA now aims for full employment instead

problems.detail: The RBA's 2023 Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy dropped the wording 'on average, over time'. The target is now annual CPI inflation of 2 to 3%, with a focus on the 2.5% midpoint. The card still treats it as a medium-term, flexible target, which is broadly right, but the 'on average' framing is out of date and the midpoint focus is missing. This wording comes from the chapter point itself.

'Some unemployment remains at this level, and the RBA calls it the maximum sustainable level of employment' is ambiguous. 'It' could be read as the remaining unemployment rather than the level of employment.

The right option is clearly the longest and the only one with the qualifier 'on average over time'. It also repeats the remember line word for word, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
